Fatality: A work-related injury resulting in death of the injured person (even if the death occurs some time later).
Lost Time Incident (LTI): A work-related injury or illness where a medical practitioner recommend that the employee stay home from work as a result of his/her injuries or illness, beginning the first work day after the incident.
Medical Treatment: A work-related injury or illness that requires treatment of a medical practitioner. This does not include visits to a medical practitioner for the purpose of diagnosis (e.g. x-rays, scans, blood tests, administration of prescription drugs for diagnostic purposes), observation or counselling or when a medical practitioner provides first aid treatment. Includes any medical treatment beyond first aid, and when the employee loses consciousness other than simple fainting.
First Aid: An incident wherein an employee requires minor medical attention, not requiring the intervention of a medical practitioner.
Lost Time Incident Frequency (LTIF): Number of LTI’s per 1 million worked hours.
Total Recordable Incidents Frequency (TRIF): Total number of recordable incidents (Fatalities, LTI’s, Restricted Work Cases and Medical Treatment) per 1 million worked hours.
All worked hours in the unit in the period of reporting, including subcontractor and agency hours for which incidents are reported to Aker Kvaerner (as defined by each project).
Work days lost due to illness. Total sick leave and long term sick leave (more than 16 consecutive days).

Energy Consumption: Oil, gas and electricity measured in MWh.
Material Usage: Steel, paint, aluminium, and titanium measured in Metric tonnes.
Emissions: CO2, NOx, SO2 and VOCs measured in Metric tonnes.
Waste: Recycled, disposed of as landfill, or other, measured in Metric tonnes.

Risk Observations: Observations of at risk behaviours and/or conditions logged through a documented system. Excluding those during planned inspections or audits.
Near Misses: Incidents that, under slightly altered circumstances, could have resulted in injury, harm or damage. Energy must be expended for a near miss to occur. 
Task Risk Analysis: Planned risk assessments linked to upcoming tasks, carried out by a team or individual prior to a specific task.  E.g. Take 2, Step Back, Task Safety Awareness, Time Out For Safety, Job Safety Analysis, Job Hazard Analysis, Task Risk Assessment etc.
Inspections: Documented inspections as part of planned HSE management programme.  Includes site walkabouts, safety tours, scorecard rounds, office inspections etc.
HSE Training: Number of hours of HSE training participation where attendance is documented and it is given in a ‘classroom’ or ‘mess room’ environment. Also includes site induction and short, non-task specific HSE training sessions to site teams.  Excludes tool-box talks carried out on the work site.
